locationPreference.mechanism: Cookie selected_location (value = option data-slug: culver-city | san-pedro), 30 days, path=/. Set when the #currently-shopping select changes (then the browser navigates to the location page) and on every page load whose path equals or sits under a location URL (/location/culver-city/... or /location/san-pedro/...). On other pages the cookie selects the option. With a selected option, main.js rewrites every .active-location-menu href to that option data-menu-url (+ data-deep-link, unused) and fills #locationAddress/#locationHours. A click on .js-selected-location-menu goes to the selected option data-menu-url, else to data-lax-url/data-sanpedro-url by cookie (culver-city|lax / san-pedro|sanpedro), else opens the location chooser modal. A click on .js-location-chooser always opens the modal, whose two cards take the trigger data-lax-url/data-sanpedro-url. The age gate is separate: localStorage agePass_v2="true" + cookie agePass_v2=true (max-age 31536000, SameSite=Lax, Secure on https); its "Shop here" links navigate to the location page, which then sets selected_location by path. If cookies are blocked the select is hidden.

risks.risk: Partner-hosted embeds may be bound to the werollup.com origin and path. Jane runtimeConfig carries partnerHostedPath "/location/san-pedro/shop" and embed config 989 is a partner-hosted config, presumably registered for werollup.com (nothing on disk shows Jane origin settings); Jane may reject API calls from another origin (CORS) or mis-route when the page is not at that exact path (for example a Pages preview under /<repo>/...). The Weedmaps script lives on the store subdomain werolluplax.wm.store and may check the embedding origin. A preview on another host may therefore show no menu.
risks.test: only on the operator-approved preview or the production cutover, in a real browser; do not probe the vendors from this workspace

risks.risk: In the harvest headless Chrome (tools/capture-live.mjs, which does not block iheartjane or wm.store) neither menu painted: San Pedro #app box height 0 at 1440 (audit/capture/baseline.location-san-pedro-shop.1440.style.json) and the screenshots show an empty area under the Culver City hero and nothing under the San Pedro and /lax-menu heroes (audit/screens/source/*shop*.1440.png, lax-menu.1440.png). Headless QA of the rebuild cannot prove the menus work, and an empty #app in QA is not by itself a regression.
risks.test: compare like with like: the live page and the rebuild in the same browser mode

risks.risk: The Jane module URL is content-hashed (index-D8IbwKpn.js) and the header block is generated by Jane at request time (comment: "See api/app/lib/embed/html/build.rb"). A static snapshot freezes this hash and the settings JSON; when Jane deploys a new build the old asset may be removed from boost-assets.iheartjane.com and the San Pedro menu goes blank. Nothing on disk shows Jane retention policy.
risks.test: none possible offline; mitigation = a documented refresh step (re-copy the Jane header block from a fresh fetch, operator-approved) or a server-side include

risks.risk: Age gate vs embed: until agePass_v2 is found, #mainContent carries .hidden-content (visibility:hidden; opacity:0, aria-hidden=true) and body overflow is hidden; the embeds sit inside #mainContent. Scripts still load while hidden. After the pass the inline script removes .hidden-content. The rebuild must keep the menu container inside the revealed region, must not lazy-load the vendor scripts behind an IntersectionObserver that never fires while hidden, and must not add a second gate. Jane runtimeConfig sets showAgeGate:false, so the site gate is the only gate for San Pedro; whether the Weedmaps store shows its own gate is UNVERIFIED.
risks.test: functional QA: fresh profile -> pass gate -> choose store -> menu container visible and not zero-height (subject to R2)

risks.risk: Payment and checkout run inside the vendor apps: jane-app-settings names Square (web.squarecdn.com), Moneris (gateway.moneris.com), CanPay (remotepay.canpaydebit.com), Aeropay and Stronghold. The rebuild needs nothing for them except not blocking them: no restrictive Content-Security-Policy, no sandboxing, no blocking of third-party scripts on the shop pages. Whether the live site sends a CSP is UNVERIFIED (the crawl stored only 5 response headers).
risks.test: header check on the built host

risks.risk: Deep links: 47 of the 91 crawled pages are shop variants (18 Culver City query variants, 8 San Pedro /shop/menu/<category> paths, 19 San Pedro ?filters variants, plus the 2 base shop pages; /lax-menu separately). Query variants need no extra files; the 8 menu paths need served pages. Jane can generate further sub-paths while a visitor browses (not in the crawl; the Jane sitemap at /media/jane-menu/sitemap.xml was not saved), so without a catch-all a reload or shared link of such a URL returns 404 on a static host.
risks.test: link-check every inventory URL on the build; request one unknown sub-path such as /location/san-pedro/shop/menu/does-not-exist and confirm the fallback boots the embed

risks.risk: Secret scanning: jane-app-secrets and jane-app-settings carry vendor public client keys (Google API keys of the AIza form, Mapbox pk., Algolia search key, Mixpanel/Braze/Datadog tokens). They are served to every visitor of the live page and are not the operator keys of PLAN D7, but a scanner will match them. Allowlist these exact strings for the San Pedro shop pages only; do not loosen the scanner globally.
risks.test: run tools/secret-scan.mjs on dist with the allowlist and a positive control

risks.risk: Primary-navigation pages (40) list "Order Vaporizers & Cartridges" under the San Pedro group with href /shop-playa-vista/?filters%5Broot_types%5D%5B%5D=vape, which lands on the Culver City (Weedmaps) shop with the filter dropped. Carry verbatim by default (PLAN D2); fixing it to /location/san-pedro/shop/?filters%5Broot_types%5D%5B%5D=vape (the href the San Pedro menu itself uses) needs operator approval.

Canonicals: live San Pedro variants carry their own canonical (sub-path or query kept, e.g. https://werollup.com/location/san-pedro/shop/?filters%5Bfeelings%5D%5B%5D=Pain+Free) while Culver City variants all point to /location/culver-city/shop/. One static file per path cannot vary its canonical by query string; the generated /shop/menu/<cat>/ copies can keep theirs. Hand to the SEO lane.

Location preference JS quirks to preserve or consciously drop: .active-location-menu also matches the footer <li id="menu-item-62041"> (main.js sets .href on the LI, a no-op, and sets display:inherit); data-deep-link support exists but no element uses it; if cookies are disabled the #currently-shopping select is hidden.
